messages:
sam: Heads-up - we see a perf regression on the LL proto path when running multi-GPU with hybrid channels + small batches. Throughput drops ~28% compared to previous week.

julia: reproable on 8xA100? which model/seq len?

sam: 8xA100, mix of tensor+pipeline (tp=2, pp=1), seq=1024 typical, kv cache enabled. Affected when batch_size<4.

maria: can you paste the perf trace?

sam: pasted perf-bot link: https://perf.internal/runs/1973456789 - main anomalies: frequent allreduce stalls, long tail on ncclSend/NcclRecv, and kernel selector picks non-fused ffw kernels for some blocks.

perf-bot: Profiling summary (quick):
- collector: nvprof + custom tracer
- spike windows around step 120-140
- 62% of stall time in point-to-point wait after allreduce
- kernel selection: 18% of time in unfused GEMM variant vs fused in baseline
- KV prefetch shows repeated cache miss eviction pattern

ryan: sounds like channel starvation + small microbatches causing faulty scheduling. Are we using LL128 channels?

sam: yes LL128 enabled on the cluster for these queues. Interestingly, when I flip to LL (non-128) the regression goes away but latency increases overall.

julia: did we change algo/proto policy recently? there was an automated change in the kernel selector last week to prefer proto for small collectives.

sam: the rollout note shows proto-prefer for small msg sizes on the cluster pool used.

maria: hypothesis: LL128 + proto together increases per-channel contention with many small messages -> driver queues more small allreduces concurrently -> scheduler defers compute kernels -> exposes kernel selector fallback to unfused kernels because of different occupancy?

ryan: +1. Also KV cache prefetch might interleave CPU memcpy and GPU transfers causing additional bursts. Prefetch writes small KV entries then triggers many small inter-node collectives.

sam: here's the minimal reproduce snippet I used: 
```
export NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE=PARALLEL
export NCCL_PROTO=LL
export NCCL_ALGO=RING
# try LL128 on/off
export NCCL_LL128_ENABLE=1
python serve_benchmark.py --gpus 8 --tp 2 --pp 1 --batch 2 --seq 1024 --kv-prefetch
```

julia: try flipping NCCL_PROTO=PROTO with LL128=1 and measure? also disable prefetch to see delta.

sam: ran quick matrix: 
- proto+ll128: throughput -32% vs baseline
- proto only (ll128=0): -15%
- llproto off (NCCL_PROTO=LL): baseline throughput (regression gone)
- kv-prefetch off reduces regression to -8%

maria: that pattern implies interaction between proto path and packetization on LL128. Proto seems to generate extra rounds for some collectives which increases small-msg overhead.

ryan: actionable ideas: 
1) add heuristic: when kv-prefetch OR batch_size < 4, prefer NCCL_PROTO=LL or disable LL128 (avoid proto+LL128 combo)
2) force fused kernel selection when occupancy lower than threshold (we saw unfused fallback)
3) throttle prefetch concurrency so we don't spawn many small collectives at once

sam: I can implement quick runtime switch in kernel selector to prefer fused kernels if running with small batches and kv enabled. Will try today.

julia: please also collect nccl debug traces (NCCL_DEBUG=INFO) and system trace (nsys) for next run. Upload to perf link.

perf-bot: Note: added benchmark job 1973456795 capturing nccl debug + nsys; upload ETA ~10m.

maria: if tests confirm, we should ship a targeted fallback policy on the routing layer: detect small-batch kv-heavy sessions and route them to LL path or different channel config.

ryan: agree. Also add an integration test in nightly that exercises proto+ll128 + kv-prefetch small batch to prevent regressions.

sam: quick status update after making fused-kernel preference change: preliminary runs show throughput recovered to within 6% of baseline; still investigating tail.

julia: nice. keep the proto/ll128 matrix and perf traces in the issue. I'll start a follow-up PR for a safe rollout strategy for proto heuristics.

maria: nice triage. assign to sam for fixes and ryan for routing heuristics.

sam: assigning and will post final traces to the perf link when done. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
